findings.what: This is the point the corrector raised. The sentence 'a set almost invariant under a dense subgroup of a group acting continuously and ergodically is null or conull' states, as a general fact, Mathlib's aeconst_of_dense_aestabilizer_smul without its side conditions: X an R1 Borel space, the measure finite and inner regular, the inverse continuous. Taken alone, the fact is false. Take R acting on itself by translation with counting measure. The action is continuous and ergodic (the only invariant sets are the empty set and R), Q is dense, and the Q-invariant set Q is neither null nor conull. In context the measure is lambda on S^d, a finite Borel measure on a compact metric space, so every side condition holds there. The claim the paragraph makes (density => ergodicity on S^d, d >= 1) is exactly EGF.isGroupErgodic_sphereRotGroup_of_dense. So the paper claims no more than is proved, but one step of the proof is stated more generally than it holds. The text is C-53's adopted text, which the corrector applied verbatim.

findings.what: The paragraph proves h ergodic for 'A a measurable set invariant under h' and closes with 'A set invariant under the group is invariant under each of its elements, so one ergodic element makes the group ergodic'. Definition 3.1 (l.233), the ergodicity Theorem 3.5 assumes, concerns sets almost invariant under the generators (lambda(Phi_i^{-1}A symdiff A) = 0). Read strictly, the last step also needs the standard fact that an ergodic map has no non-trivial almost invariant set, which the text does not state. The Lean takes it from QuasiErgodic.ae_empty_or_univ0 in isGroupErgodic_of_ergodic_mem, and its Fourier criterion already assumes f o h = f a.e. (ergodic_of_mFourierCoeff). Read as 'almost invariant' throughout, the paragraph is correct as written. The Fourier identity needs only a.e. invariance, and B.2's C-28 sentence (l.895) uses 'invariant' the same way. Wording only: nothing is claimed beyond the Lean.

findings.what: This is the corrector's l.260 point. It is real but not an overclaim, and it is not this batch's round 2. l.260 says 'Ergodicity guarantees, for a model rich enough (Theorem 3.4), that the parameterized family of EGFs is universal ... such as affine maps on tori and rotations on spheres'. That is the use C-54 corrects at l.338. l.260 echoes Theorem 3.4 (l.305), 'A parameterized family of EGF is universal provided ...'. Both stay true: a family whose members are all EGFs is a special case, and such families exist with affine maps and rotations (frozen ergodic moves). But 'of EGF' is a hypothesis the Lean does not need: EGF.universality_of_ergodic_family holds for any family of generative flows. After C-54 the affine toroidal and isometry spherical families are families of generative flows with some members EGFs, so they meet Theorem 3.4's wording only through the family, not member by member. B.2 and B.3 derive Theorems 3.5-3.6 from Theorem B.1, not from 3.4, so no proof breaks. The batch makes no statement false and changes no symbol's meaning. Neither line is among C-54's `printed` (v1 l.238, l.277 are C-18/C-29/C-20/C-50 sites), so the corrector was right to leave them.
